prompt: We hold ISO 27001:2022 certification. Do we still need TISAX for our VW contract, and how much extra work is it?
assertions: Answers the core question correctly: yes — ISO 27001 certification does NOT substitute for TISAX; OEMs like VW contractually require TISAX labels, and TISAX is an assessment/label regime on the ENX platform, not a certificate
Quantifies the head start credibly: roughly 70-80% control overlap with ISO 27001, so the certified ISMS (policies, risk register, evidence) is the best starting point

Names the real deltas: fixed maturity targets with CUTBACK scoring (no SoA-style tailoring — every applicable question must reach target maturity 3), High/Very-High additional requirements, the prototype-protection module where in scope, and ENX label/exchange mechanics (3-year validity, corrective windows)

Recommends the right workflow: map existing ISO evidence to ISA control areas first, re-express evidence in maturity terms (ISO 'implemented' is only maturity 3 when established and demonstrably operating), then close automotive-specific gaps — one ISMS, not a parallel programme

Mentions assessment mechanics accurately: objectives determine the assessment level (AL2/AL3), assessment by an ENX-accredited audit provider, results shared with VW via the ENX platform at a chosen disclosure level
